# Business & Industry — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Other Business & Industry Items: typically around 900, most listings 200–24,000 (29 listings)
- Industry Machinery & Tools: typically around 65,000, most listings 6,000–245,000 (9 listings)
- Raw Materials & Industrial Supplies: typically around 400, most listings 200–3,000 (6 listings)
- Safety & Security: typically around 2,500, most listings 2,000–9,500 (6 listings)

Machinery is the high-value subcategory: a generator, mill, or industrial machine priced far below what its type sells for (well under the ~6,000 floor, or a fraction of comparable machines) is a scam signal → hold. Every row except "Other" has n < 10 — the bands are thin, so lean on general judgment of what the specific item should cost. Licences, Titles & Tenders has only 3 listings (no usable range); judge those case by case.

## What good listings look like
Real approved examples (the sample pool here is small and mostly miscategorized; only these fit the category):
- "Smoke detectors Alarm" — NPR 2,400 (Safety & Security)
- "Sunflower oil" — NPR 2,750 (bulk supply)

A good listing names the equipment or material type, brand and capacity/spec (kVA, tonnage, size), condition, and — for raw materials — the quantity or unit the price covers.

## Category-specific hold signals
- This category is a frequent wrong-category dumping ground — real approved samples include phones ("eg.REDMI A5 128", iPhone X camera parts), furniture ("Modern bed"), bouquets, gifts, and sports gear. An obvious consumer item posted under Business & Industry → hold for recategorization.
- Promo/redirect spam appears here (real sample: "daraz 6/3 80% discount only for few days"). A listing advertising another platform's discounts or deals instead of selling a specific item → hold.
- Licences, Titles & Tenders: legitimate posts transfer a licence together with a running business or asset. A bare government licence offered "for sale", or promises of guaranteed tenders/contracts → hold.
